[LUNI.4.1.5] **A dimension or a unit is its declaration.** The compiler must treat each
`unit dimension` and `unit scalar` declaration as one dimension or scalar group
of its own. Two declarations are two, whatever their names, storage types and
units, so a value of one meeting a value of the other is [LUNI.8.2]'s error. A
file that imports a declaration holds that declaration: `units.customary`'s
`psi` and `units.si`'s `pascal` share `pressure`, which `units.customary` imports.

Each unit symbol's declaration is one unit of its own, with its own scale and
label ([LUNI.4.3], [LUNI.11.2]). Two libraries' `mark`s in one dimension are two
units: a value of one meeting a value of the other converts as any two units of
a dimension do ([LUNI.8.1]), and `x::mark` naming the other is no identity
([LCST.4.5.1]), so the compiler must refuse it ([LCST.4.5.3]). A slot or a
constant holds the unit its declaring file resolved ([LIMP.1.5]).

A dimension, a scalar group, a unit and an opaque type have no own name
([LIMP.13.1]). A slot's artefact holds its kind ([RDSC.5.5.4]), and nothing past
the source tells two of them apart.
